neighbours.label: Auxiliary do / does / did in a reply that confirms what the previous speaker just said, with or without the verb ('“He loves it.” “He does love it”'); the same auxiliary with no previous speaker, and replies with a different verb, stay lower.
fire: “She adores that old piano.” “She does adore it,” he said.
“You really like this town.” “I do like it,” she told him.
“They bought a boat last year.” “They did buy one,” I said.
“It looks expensive to me.” “It does look expensive,” he agreed.
“He finished the whole report.” “He did finish it,” she said.
Rob: You seem worried about it. Ann: I do worry, yes.
“Your son plays very well.” “He does play well,” she smiled.
Tim: This soup tastes odd. Eve: It does taste odd, yeah.
